Q: How to download and install a Git client for Windows using PowerShell A:

You can script the installation of Git using Chocolatey.

The package is documented at Chocolatey's Git package page.

  1. First, you must install Chocolatey, but that can be done on the command line.

  2. Then the command is:

    choco install -y git

Q: QtWidget setSizePolicy called with wrong argument types A:

Problem makes .sizeHint() in .setSizePolicy().
Function .sizeHint() is not for setting SizePolicy.

You have to keep only lines with QtWidgets.QSizePolicy.Policy.Fixed - for all buttons.

If you print value from .sizeHint() then you see something like PyQt6.QtCore.QSize(80, 23)
but QtWidgets.QSizePolicy.Policy.Fixed displays Policy.Fixed

Doc for other allowed values: QSizePolicy.Policy

Minimal working code for tests:

import sys
from PyQt6 import QtWidgets


class Window(QtWidgets.QWidget):

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

        layout = QtWidgets.QHBoxLayout(self)

        button = QtWidgets.QPushButton("Home")

        # set fixed size policy
        button.setSizePolicy(
            QtWidgets.QSizePolicy.Policy.Fixed, QtWidgets.QSizePolicy.Policy.Fixed
        )

        layout.addWidget(button)

        print(button.sizeHint())
        print(QtWidgets.QSizePolicy.Policy.Fixed)


app = QtWidgets.QApplication(sys.argv)

window = Window()
window.show()

app.exec()

Q: Change the legend labels to include sub- AND superscript expression on facetted data A:

To keep the 'default' ggplot2 colour scheme, one potential option specifying 'labels' for the colour scale via scale_colour_hue() (using the built-in mtcars dataset):

mtcars %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=disp, y=hp, colour=factor(cyl),
             group = factor(cyl), shape=factor(gear))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ carb, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_colour_hue(labels = c("4" = "HCL",
                                 "6" = bquote("H"[2]*"SO"[4]),
                                 "8" = bquote("Fe"^"2+"+"H"[2]*"SO"[4])))

Q: Implementing a custom comparer that treats the numbers as integers rather than strings A:

Like Dale K, I'm puzzled as to where you got the idea that "Microsft" (I assume you mean C#/.NET specifically?) sorts numbers as text. If you have a list of numbers, the standard sort will sort them numerically.

The following code:

List<int> numbers = new List<int> { 1, 11, 2, 3, 10 };
numbers.Sort();

foreach (var number in numbers)
{
  Console.WriteLine(number);
}

will output

1
2
3
10
11

Live demo: https://dotnetfiddle.net/PxYQZW

You don't need a custom comparer for this task - the AI on DuckDuckGo that you linked to is hallucinating (or possibly not doing good enough research).

Of course if you had a list of strings then you'd get a different result:

List<string> numbers = new List<string> {"1", "11", "2", "3", "10" };
numbers.Sort();

foreach (var number in numbers)
{
  Console.WriteLine(number);
}

outputs

1
10
11
2
3

Live demo: https://dotnetfiddle.net/ejXn7e

Maybe this is a scenario you've been in at some point which led you the conclusion that numbers are always sorted as text?? In this case that's only because, as far as the program is concerned, they are just text. Data types are important.

You could use a custom comparer to change that output, but of course a far more sensible solution would be simply to have the list be of type int to begin with, as above.

As to your actual question, and regardless of the use of the custom comparer or not, I'm a bit perplexed. It's not clear, in the code you provided, where the list of numbers really originates from, or how that relates in any way to your SQL query. Into which field are you hoping to insert the number (or numbers??)? At the moment you don't attempt to do anything at all with the numbers list after it's been sorted.

Q: How to get the project name when creating an item template in Visual Studio? A:

  • According to the MS documentation "projectname: The name provided by the user when the project was created. This parameter applies only to project templates."

    So its not a valid parameter for item templates.
